kill_fact: No kill. Every load-bearing bear fact verifies against primary sources: Q2 2026 consolidated C1 cash cost of $2.42/lb ran ABOVE the maintained $2.15-$2.35 full-year guide; Xavantina mined-gold C1 printed $1,586/oz against a full-year guide that was itself RAISED to $1,100-$1,350/oz with AISC raised to $2,200-$2,700/oz; capital guidance was raised $10M to $285-$330M and the CFO volunteered a further potential $20-$25M of FX/inflation impact plus ~$0.10/lb on consolidated copper C1 (all CFO Wayne Drier / CEO Makko DeFilippo, 6 Aug 2026 call); trailing free cash flow is $153.5M on a $3.72bn market value (4.13% yield) earned with copper at $6.6385/lb, 13.4% above its 200-day of $5.856 and 1.3% off its 52-week high; and the shareholder-return step is still undelivered with the stated gate moved from deleveraging to revolver paydown ($95M outstanding as of the 6 Aug 2026 call). What DOES break is the record's second valuation leg: the 'completely independent check' that supposedly lands in the same place as the sum-of-the-parts was computed on mismatched EBITDA bases and, corrected, lands at $35.02/share, essentially at the market price, not at $32. The bear conclusion (no margin of safety at $35.65) survives the correction; the corroboration that was said to confirm it does not.
corrections: (1) NUMBERS, material. The peer-multiple cross-check applies the peer median EV/EBITDA of ~7.3x (Ero 7.33 / Hudbay 7.32 / Capstone 7.09 -- all struck on vendor TTM-EBITDA) to $533M of COMPANY-ADJUSTED trailing EBITDA (the CFO's number on the 6 Aug 2026 call, which excludes FX and derivative gains). Mismatched bases. On the basis the multiples were actually struck, Ero's trailing EBITDA is $572.5M (implied twice over by net debt $471.6M / net-debt-to-EBITDA 0.8237 and by EV $4,190.5M / EV-to-EBITDA 7.3194 at 11 Aug 2026). Like-for-like: 7.3 x $572.5M = $4,179M EV, less $471.6M net debt = $3,707M / 105,876,946 diluted shares = $35.02/share. Note the method is near-tautological anyway -- a name sitting exactly at the peer median must value at roughly its own price -- so it never was independent confirmation. Averaging the unchanged sum-of-the-parts ($31.50) with the corrected peer leg ($35.02) re-derives base fair value at $33.25. The bear's own framing survives: at $35.65 there is still no margin of safety, and the 'no relative discount to harvest' claim is if anything reinforced (Ero 7.33x vs a 7.325x median). (2) CATALYST, factual. The record states 'A Capital Markets Day was promised for mid-September on the 6 March 2026 call; no date had been confirmed as of the 5 August 2026 release' and 'There is no hard-dated event that forces a re-rating.' Both are stale by one day: the CEO confirmed the date twice on the 6 Aug 2026 call -- 'hosting our Capital Markets Day in Sao Paulo on Monday, September 14' -- and separately committed to 'come back to the market later this year' on shareholder returns once the revolver step is met. A dated corporate event sits ~5 weeks out. This does not change the SOFT_EXTENDED read (no contractual payout) and per lane rules is descriptive only. (3) CONSENSUS EVIDENCE, material to the argument, not to a level. The 'only four price targets in the past twelve months / trades above every posted target' claim is a vendor-coverage artifact, not a market fact: the aggregator carries 4 targets sourced from two news scrapers (TheFly, StreetInsider) and a single $31 consensus, while EIGHT brokers asked questions on the 6 Aug 2026 call (BMO, BofA, TD Cowen, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, Cormark, Scotiabank, Bradesco). 'Above every published street target' is unverified and probably false; the record should not lean on it as evidence that the re-rating has outrun the street. (4) RESERVE FOOTNOTE, minor. The record asserts a 'roughly 12-year mine life' for Tucuma. On the 6 Aug 2026 call Craig Hutchison (TD Cowen) noted the Tucuma reserve report is roughly five years old and the CEO confirmed 'We do expect to publish a technical report on Tucuma this year.' The mine-life input is a pre-2022 filing struck at roughly half today's copper price; direction of any restatement is more likely up than down, so it is a staleness flag, not a downgrade. (5) NO HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER FOUND. No equity dilution (diluted shares 103.9M at Q1 2025 to 105.877M at 30 Jun 2026, ~2%), no permit issue, no undisclosed reserve cut. One unresolved item: $100.7M of deferred revenue sits on the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet ($11.6M current + $89.1M non-current) OUTSIDE the $452.7M net-debt figure. If that is the Royal Gold precious-metals stream, the record already captures its economics by deducting ~$27M/yr from the Xavantina line and no adjustment is due; if any part of it is the copper prepayment facility, the net-debt deduction is understated by up to ~$0.95/share. Could not split it from the primary filing text within this pass -- flagged, not corrected, so as not to double-count.
